resources.notes: 66 distinct esearch queries executed against eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov; every esearch, esummary and efetch call returned HTTP 200 with parseable JSON/text. No rate-limiting (429) encountered at ~1 req/0.5 s without an API key. PubMed is a bibliographic index only: it yielded no primary data files, so every hit was carried to Europe PMC / PMC for full text and supplements. Relevance filtering required BOTH an oligonucleotide term and a platelet/thrombocytopenia term in the title; identifier list is the union of de-duplicated relevant PMIDs across all queries. Several priority targets returned genuinely empty result sets, which is a real finding and not a barrier: '(eteplirsen OR golodirsen OR viltolarsen OR casimersen) AND (platelet OR platelets OR thrombocytopenia)' = 0 hits; 'morpholino oligomer AND (thrombocytopenia OR platelet OR coagulation)' = 8 hits none relevant; 'mipomersen AND (platelet OR platelets OR thrombocytopenia)' = 1 hit, not a per-trial platelet report. The neutral-backbone PMO class therefore has NO indexed platelet-endpoint literature in PubMed - the only routes are the casimersen RCT safety tables (PMID 34105177) and the eteplirsen FAERS disproportionality analysis (PMID 39027557).

resources.barrier_detail: The documented FULL_TEXT: field index is non-functional for this account/endpoint. 'FULL_TEXT:"platelet activation"' returned HTTP 200 with hitCount 0; 'FULL_TEXT:"antisense oligonucleotide" AND FULL_TEXT:"platelet activation" AND FULL_TEXT:"glycoprotein VI"' returned HTTP 200 hitCount 0; 'FULL_TEXT:oligonucleotide AND FULL_TEXT:"washed human platelets"' returned HTTP 200 hitCount 0; 'FULL_TEXT:"phosphorothioate" AND FULL_TEXT:"platelet-rich plasma" AND FULL_TEXT:thrombocytopenia' returned HTTP 200 hitCount 0. No error body was returned - the field silently matches nothing. Workaround applied and verified: the same phrases run UNFIELDED do search full text (e.g. '"washed human platelets" AND oligonucleotide' = 61 hits; 'cASO7 OR cASO9 OR cASO11' = 22 hits and surfaced the target paper as rank 1). All reported Europe PMC hits come from the unfielded form.
resources.notes: 28 distinct queries, all HTTP 200. Europe PMC was decisive for two things PubMed could not do: (1) unfielded full-text matching resolved the control-ASO sequence source from a bare DOI and from the literal strings cASO7/cASO9/cASO11 to PMID 42733805 / PMC13571576; (2) the isOpenAccess and hasSuppl flags in resultType=core let me triage which candidates have a legally retrievable supplement before attempting any download. Note hasSuppl=Y does not imply a data file: Flierl 2015 (PMC4322051) hasSuppl=Y but the supplementaryFiles archive contains only figure JPG/GIF renditions, no data table.

notes:
SCOPE AND HONESTY STATEMENT. Family = literature_core only (PubMed via NCBI E-utilities, and Europe PMC via its REST API). All searches ran on 2026-10-02. 66 distinct PubMed esearch queries and 28 distinct Europe PMC queries were executed; every one returned HTTP 200. Neither service was blocked, rate-limited or login-gated at any point, and no CAPTCHA was encountered. No account was created, nothing was purchased, no credentials were supplied, and no author was contacted.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN HAND (not merely cited). Eight files were downloaded from legally open routes and written to the staging directory with bytes and sha256 recorded in files_written below. The four that matter most: (1) Sewing 2017 full text plus its S1 raw-data workbook; (2) Lundberg-Slingsby 2022 full text plus its 542 kB online supplementary appendix; (3) Flierl 2015 full text; (4) the complete Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids 2026 supplement, from which mmc1.pdf was extracted and Table S2 verified on page 20 - it gives the exact sequences and per-linkage modification notation for control ASOs cASO1-cASO17, including the three named in the task (cASO7, cASO9, cASO11, all 20-nt uniform 2'-MOE/PS). That resolves the control-sequence target completely. Zaslavsky 2021 was recovered as a free NIHMS author manuscript after Europe PMC's endpoint failed on it.

RANKING RATIONALE. The challenge prioritises human in vitro / ex vivo systems and raw per-donor data over additional clinical rows, and states that row count is not a qualification criterion. I have therefore ranked priority 1 as the nine items that measure something on HUMAN platelets: Sewing 2017 (human platelets, GPVI and PF4 binding, chemistry SAR by length and PS count, raw workbook in hand), Lundberg-Slingsby 2022 (human donor platelets, sequence-specific GPVI activation, supplement in hand), Flierl 2015 (human platelets plus platelets from GPVI-function-deficient PATIENTS - a human genetic control nothing else supplies), Zaslavsky 2021 (healthy donors AND prostate cancer patients, 6-8-fold P-selectin increase, TLR7-dependent and PS-INDEPENDENT, i.e. a second mechanism), Harada 2024 (human PRP and whole blood under shear in a microphysiological system with endothelium, oligonucleotide ODN2395, SYK-rescuable), the pelacarsen ARU/PRU paper (ex vivo platelet function in 275 trial subjects, and a NEGATIVE result - the discriminating counter-example), Crooke 2017 (the 2,638-subject 16-ASO denominator that de-pools the class and shows 3 of 16 sequences carry the signal), the TLR panel in human whole blood under flow, and the recovered cASO chemistry table. Every clinical trial series - oblimersen, aprinocarsen, ISIS 5132, alicaforsen, drisapersen, mipomersen, donidalorsen, nusinersen - is ranked 2 or 3 BELOW those, deliberately, because they add rows of the kind the challenge says it is not counting.

GENUINE NEGATIVE FINDINGS, recorded as findings rather than dressed up as barriers. The direct query '(eteplirsen OR golodirsen OR viltolarsen OR casimersen) AND (platelet OR platelets OR thrombocytopenia)' returns COUNT=0 in PubMed (HTTP 200, verified empty). 'morpholino oligomer AND (thrombocytopenia OR platelet OR coagulation)' returns 8 hits, none relevant. So the PMO neutral-backbone comparator - the control that makes the PS/GPVI mechanism interpretable - has no platelet-focused literature at all; the only free routes are indirect (casimersen RCT haematology appendix PMC9290993, eteplirsen FAERS disproportionality PMC11255655), and any row drawn from them is a null finding from a generic safety table, which must be labelled as such. 'mipomersen AND (platelet OR platelets OR thrombocytopenia)' returns only 1 hit, so mipomersen platelet values sit inside generic safety tables and extraction will be table-level, not keyword-driven. Likewise, the named CS20/CS21 alicaforsen phase 3 Crohn's reports and the named NURTURE/SHINE/DEVOTE nusinersen trial publications were NOT surfaced as primary publications by any query in either database; their NCT numbers verify but their papers did not appear, and I have not substituted something else and called it the same thing.

BARRIERS, with exact symptoms. Publisher paywall confirmed by response body for the pelacarsen platelet-reactivity paper (link.springer.com, 344,559-byte landing page carrying 'Access this article', 'Buy article', 'USD 39'). Elsevier served a 2,664-byte interstitial with meta name=tdm-reservation content=1 instead of the Thrombosis Research full text. Technical blocks: Europe PMC's documented FULL_TEXT: field index silently returns hitCount 0 for every phrase at HTTP 200 (four queries tested) - worked around by running the same phrases unfielded, which does search full text and which surfaced the cASO paper from the literal strings cASO7/cASO9/cASO11; Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 for the one NIHMS author manuscript (PMC8264460) and an empty 296-byte supplement archive for it; there is no per-file selection on supplementaryFiles, so a 28 MB archive had to be pulled for one table, and that transfer was truncated twice by client timeouts before completing on a 560 s retry; europepmc.org/articles/PMC13571576/bin/mmc1.pdf returned HTTP 403 and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/instance/13571576/bin/mmc1.pdf returned HTTP 200 but with content_type text/html and 1,817 bytes (an error page, not the PDF). Broken link: the legacy NCBI PMC OA Web Service oa.fcgi returned HTTP 404 with a 1,584-byte 'NCBI/xpmc21 - WWW Error 404 Diagnostic' page for all three ids tried, including PMC5673186, which is demonstrably in the OA subset - so the endpoint is retired, not the articles missing.

UNRESOLVED / UNVERIFIABLE. PMID 15027323 (Shoji 2004, human platelet ASO uptake in healthy volunteers vs thrombocytopenic patients) has no DOI and no PMCID in Europe PMC, so there is no open endpoint to attempt and no identifier beyond the PMID to report; it is recorded as abstract-only rather than as a paywall, because I did not reach a paywall.
